composition: top nav bar and a second 'On this page' bar stacked inside a drawing-sheet frame
large empty page area below, leaving the nav as the only content
title block in the bottom right of the sheet
mobile menu panel on the right as its own sheet with the same zone border
zone numbers 1-3 on top and bottom, letters A-C down the sides
layout_devices: small superscript numerals 01-07 above each nav label
thin vertical dividers between nav items
CTA button wrapped in corner brackets and square brackets
active section tab outlined with a dot marker and steel-blue underline
segmented page-progress bar with percentage and revision letter
mobile section-jump list with arrow markers on the active row
dashed vertical fold line between desktop and mobile
palette: deep navy text, rules and frame
steel-blue filled CTA button and active tab tint
typography: mono caps for all nav and section labels
geometric bold sans wordmark with tiny caps tagline
mono figures for progress and revision
rendering: UI mockup with no device frame
motion_implied: progress bar segments fill as you scroll
active tab marker slides between sections
arrow markers nudge on the active row
corner brackets snap around the CTA on hover
t2i_keywords: numbered menu items with superscript index
zone numbers and letters along the edges
t2i_prompt: Flat UI mockup, no device frame, of <CONTENT> navigation set inside an engineering drawing sheet. Warm off-white limestone background, deep navy 1 px rules, one steel-blue accent for the call-to-action button and the active state. A top bar with mono uppercase labels each carrying a small superscript index number, thin vertical dividers, a button framed by corner brackets; beneath it a secondary bar with numbered section tabs, the active one outlined with a dot, and a segmented progress bar. Sheet border with zone numbers and letters, title block bottom right, a mobile menu panel beside it. Square corners, no shadows, generous empty space.
signature_idea: Navigation as the header of a drawing sheet: numbered tabs, a revision-and-progress readout, and the page itself framed by zone references.
strengths: numbering creates a shared index system across nav, sections and footer
progress readout is a genuinely useful long-page aid
clear active state and mobile section jump
weaknesses: all-mono caps nav is dense and less legible than sentence-case sans
bracketed CTA and zone letters risk gimmick when repeated
full-sheet frame on every page could feel heavy
brand_fit_why: Navy/limestone with one steel-blue accent, square corners and mono figures are on brand; uppercase mono everywhere is heavier than the Geist light voice.
